content:
Sam H: Heads-up - proposal: add /v1/tokens/introspect to API so console and infra can resolve effective_project for service-account impersonation flows. Need to decide routing affinity (key vs effective_project) and quota attribution. cc @Jia L @Rosie :eyes:

Jia L: +1 for introspect endpoint. Important for routing fallback to dedicated pools. Question: should introspect return project_id and original_issuer? We need immutable claim to avoid spoofing.

Michael P: we must ensure introspect only returns canonicalized project and sa_id, and include ttl, scopes, and a signature. No PII. Also rate-limit the endpoint heavily.

Rosie: For console UX - if we show "effective project" in the key details, we need a clear affordance for rotation and rebind. Users confuse "service account owner" vs "billing project". Let's add labels: Issuer / Bound Project / Effective Project.

Sam H: proposed schema (very small):
```
GET /v1/tokens/introspect?token=...
200 {
  "active": true,
  "issuer": "sa-123",
  "effective_project": "proj-abc",
  "scopes": ["inference:generate"],
  "expires_at": 1712345678
}
```

Jia L: Suggest including `routing_affinity` enum: KEY | EFFECTIVE_PROJECT | ORG. Runtime will compute final route by policy; console shows current policy.

Michael P: If you include ORG, careful: quota attribution vs cost center mismatch. Need ledger mapping. Also, token exchange flows must carry original_project claim.

Rosie: UX for rotation - show a "Rebind" button that lets users choose which project to attribute. We should warn about quota implications. Maybe show estimated quota charges for each choice.

infra-bot: deploy/pipeline #4567 started for `introspect-service` canary to region eu-west-1 :rocket:

Sam H: Can we canary the policy change separately from the introspect endpoint? I'd prefer endpoint first, then policy rollout (2-step) so we can back out policy without touching introspect.

Jia L: Agreed. Plan: canary introspect in eu-west-1 with read-only, then add routing_affinity header opt-in to route engine behind feature flag.

Michael P: Also add telemetry events: token.introspect, token.route.resolve with fields: decision, latency, fallback. Put them in per-tenant logs, anonymized.

Rosie: Console needs a "who would be billed?" preview that's computed via introspect+policy simulator. UX team can prototype by EOW.

Sam H: Tests: unit for decoding claims, e2e for canary region with simulated SA impersonations, and load test to ensure introspect scale with 10k rps—this will be cached for 30s.

Jia L: Implementation note: cache keyed by token hash + routing_policy. Cache TTL 30s by default, configurable. Add cache hit/miss metrics.

Michael P: Security note: introspect must require caller token that has `tokens.introspect` scope OR be internal platform role. No public exposure.

Rosie: Decision: proceed with endpoint canary + console prototype + policy rollout opt-in. Action items: Sam to create PR for API, Jia to wire up runtime, Rosie to mock UX, Michael to write security guardrails.

Sam H: I'll open PR and a short ADR summarizing policy options. Thanks all :thumbsup:

console-ux: mock uploaded: https://figma.com/file/abc123/introspect-ux - includes "Rebind" modal and billing preview.

infra-bot: deploy/pipeline #4567 finished canary - monitoring looks clean :white_check_mark:

Jia L: Can we add an event `token.binding.change` when a user rebinds in console? Need to track rebind history for audits.

Michael P: yes, log audit events and keep immutable rebind records for 90 days.

Sam H: Last Q - how do we handle ephemeral tokens from exchange? Should introspect accept exchanged tokens and return original subject chain? Keep it simple: return chain up to 3 levels.

Jia L: ok cap chain length at 3, include `chain:[{issuer,project}]`.

Rosie: Great. I'll schedule user-testing with 2 product customers next week.

Sam H: closing loop: timeline - PR today, canary tomorrow, UX prototype Friday. Ping here if blockers.
